title: SGR-Bench: Benchmarking Search Agents on State-Gated Retrieval

visual_explainer.question: What does state-gated retrieval add to search-agent evaluation beyond simply finding the right website or page?
visual_explainer.takeaway: The benchmark separates source discovery from environment configuration: the agent must preserve the site-specific retrieval state under which answer-bearing evidence becomes visible.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Open-web search benchmarks centered on source discovery/traversal and browser-agent benchmarks centered on generic action execution rather than state-gated evidence exposure.

analysis.tldr: SGR-Bench isolates state-gated retrieval: search agents may find the correct specialized website yet fail because answer-bearing evidence remains hidden behind the wrong filters, views, hierarchy, scope, or time window.
analysis.problem: Existing search-agent and browser-agent benchmarks underrepresent specialized retrieval tasks where evidence becomes accessible only after configuring a source into the correct site-specific retrieval state.
analysis.core_idea: Create 100 expert-curated tasks across 12 public data ecosystems in which the agent must discover the source and establish the correct retrieval state; pair constraint-guided and goal-oriented formulations of the same underlying task to diagnose how explicit retrieval guidance changes performance.
analysis.agent_loop: Discover source → infer required site state → set filter/view/hierarchy/scope → inspect exposed evidence → update state → continue or answer
analysis.retrieval_design: The benchmark makes environment configuration part of retrieval. Evidence exposed under one state can determine the next state-setting operation, so source discovery, environment retrieval state, and answer synthesis are separable stages.
analysis.evidence: The strongest evaluated system reaches 66.18% item-level F1 while row-level correctness remains materially lower. A manual audit of 156 analyzable failed CLI trajectories attributes 37.2% to retrieval-scope drift and 27.6% to criterion mismatch, versus 10.3% to final answer composition. The error profile shows many failures occur after a relevant source has already been reached.
analysis.why_it_matters: SGR-Bench adds an environment-state axis to Agentic RAG evaluation. Internal evidence tracking cannot substitute for correctly configuring an external data system; a cleaner decomposition is source discovery × environment retrieval state × agent evidence state × policy.
limitations: The benchmark contains 100 tasks and is concentrated on specialized public data-retrieval websites.
CLI results are system-level outcomes because model and harness choices differ; they should not be read as pure model rankings.
Retrieval-state errors may depend on website stability and source-specific interaction affordances.
The benchmark diagnoses failures but does not causally identify which controller or state representation repairs them.
